text:
Maya: @maria_reno kicking off the pilot thread — want to align success criteria, data handoff, and timeline. Can you confirm the top 3 use cases so we scope evals?

Maria_Reno: thanks! Top use cases: 1) clinician note summarization for inbox triage, 2) structured extraction (meds/allergies/diagnoses), 3) triage classification for routing. Primary goal is production-quality accuracy for extraction and clear, concise summaries.

Sam: got it. For extraction we should do a 200-note annotated eval set. For summarization propose 300 notes + a small human rating panel (3-point usefulness scale). Suggested targets: extraction F1 >= 0.8, summary avg rating >= 2.5/3. Latency target: p99 < 800ms at 1-2 rps baseline.

Taylor: security notes up front: we cannot accept raw PHI in plaintext for the initial onboarding. Preferred options: (A) customer-provisioned S3 bucket in your account + cross-account role with limited read-only access, SSE-KMS; (B) de-identified CSV upload to a presigned endpoint; (C) pseudonymized dataset with IDs replaced.

Taylor: redaction guidance (example) — replace identifiers before upload:
```
PatientName -> <REDACTED_NAME>
MRN -> <REDACTED_MRN>
DOB -> <REDACTED_DOB>
SSN -> <REDACTED_SSN>
```
Also remove or hash free-text PHI tokens if possible. If you need a script we can share a small Python snippet.

Jamie: on connectivity — we can support:
- Cross-account S3 (preferred): create role arn:aws:iam::[ACCOUNT]:role/RedwoodPilotUpload and give us the ARN + external ID.
- SFTP drop for small batches.
- VPC Private pilot (requires ~2 week infra lead time + network approvals).

Jamie: example S3 upload command we can validate: `aws s3 cp deid_notes.csv s3://redwood-pilot-uploads/renaissance/ --sse aws:kms --profile customer-prod`

Maya: timeline proposal: sample data + schema by Fri (this week), annotated evals in 2 weeks, baseline model results in 3 weeks, pilot report + next steps in 5 weeks. If you need faster, tell us which milestone to compress.

Maria_Reno: we'll aim to deliver a de-identified CSV + schema by Friday. We also have an incoming security questionnaire — who's the contact for that?

Taylor: I'll lead the security questionnaire responses. Please send the doc to taylor_security@redwood.ai. For S3 we'll need the bucket policy and KMS key id for review. Also list any retention requirements.

Maya: success criteria summary I'll use in the SOW:
- Extraction: F1 >= 0.80 on the annotated eval set (200 notes)
- Summaries: avg human usefulness rating >= 2.5/3 (300 notes + raters)
- Latency: p99 < 800ms at target load
- No PII in logs / all persisted data encrypted with SSE-KMS

Maya: pricing and cost note: for the pilot we can provide a limited hosted trial (credits) to cover initial tokens; if throughput grows we'll propose a reserved capacity quote. I'll add a preliminary cost estimate once we see sample sizes.

Maria_Reno: perfect. One more ask — will Redwood redact logs automatically or do we need to scrub before upload?

Taylor: we do not accept raw PHI in customer uploads. We do automatic redaction in transit for logs (PII scrubbing) but you must deliver de-identified data for the evals. Exceptions only via an approved DPA and dedicated Private deployment.

Ops-bot: pilot-renaissance-177650 created — infra resources provisioned. Temporary credentials dispatched to Maya via DM. :robot_face:

Maya: thanks @ops-bot. I'll compile a single checklist (data, security items, eval plan, SOW draft) and share a draft with everyone by EOD tomorrow.

Sam: I'll draft eval prompts and baseline config (model variant + quantization) and drop in this thread once ready.

Maria_Reno: thanks team — we'll aim to get the de-id CSV and questionnaire to you by Friday afternoon. Appreciate the clarity. :pray:
